sense: the fifth or seventh day of the Roman month

terms.gloss: the Nones, the 5th of the month (the 7th in March, May, July and October)
evidence: Cic. Fam. 14.20: aut Nōnīs aut postrīdiē
terms.comment: The ninth day before the Ides, counting both ends (nōnus; Varro, LL 6.28, in Lewis & Short). The month’s adjective agrees with it: Nōnae Februāriae, 5 February; Nōnīs Mārtiīs, on 7 March. The days before are counted back to it: prīdiē Nōnās Jānuāriās, 4 January; ante diem tertium Nōnās Majās, 5 May.

phrases.latin: in Tusculānum nōs ventūrōs putāmus aut Nōnīs aut postrīdiē
phrases.english: we expect to reach the house at Tusculum on the Nones (of October, the 7th) or the day after

phrases.latin: Latīnae fēriae fuēre ante diem tertium Nōnās Majās
phrases.english: the Latin Festival was held on 5 May, the third day before the Nones

sources: Lewis & Short: Nonae
